title: Historia seditionis Satanae (Coptic Sedition of Satan)

details.intro:
The Historia seditionis Satanae is a unique Sahidic Coptic palimpsest fragment preserved in the Vatican Library. It narrates the pre-cosmic rebellion and refusal of Satan (here named Mastema) to obey the divine commandment to bow down and worship the newly created protoplast Adam and the Cross, culminating in a fierce cosmic battle between Satan and the Archangel Michael.

This fragment provides crucial evidence for the fusion of early Enochic/Jubilees demonology (the figure of Mastema) with the widespread Adam mythologem of the refusal to worship Adam (attested in the Greek Life of Adam and Eve, the Syriac Cave of Treasures, and the Quran, Surah 7:11–18).
details.provenance:
Language: Sahidic Coptic.
Date: Manuscript copied ca. 6th–7th century CE; composition reflects 3rd–4th century CE Egyptian Christian-Gnostic transmission.
Setting: Coptic monastic theological library.
details.manuscripts: • Primary Witness: MS Vatican, Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana, Vat. copt. 65, fol. 60v (palimpsest fragment).
